decisions.quote:
Crosby, Monin and Richardson (2008) provided eye tracking evidence that social referencing

occurs during offensive behavior, a result that failed to replicate in the original Reproducibility

Project: Psychology. Here, we used a peer reviewed experimental manipulation of protocol to

test whether Crosby and colleagues’ paradigm might provide stronger evidence for social

referencing when the current sample was made more similar to the original sample in terms of

relevant background knowledge. Overall, our results [were/were not] consistent with Crosby and

colleagues’ original findings, and we found that using this protocol [did/did not] change

participants’ behavior.
decisions.reason: The dependent record type (replication) and target original identity (Crosby, Monin, & Richardson, 2008) are confirmed by the manuscript, which reports a multilab direct replication of Crosby et al. (2008) after data collection was conducted. However, the supplied primary source for 10.17605/osf.io/yptua is a results-blind Registered Replication Report manuscript in which all empirical results, statistical values, and replication verdicts remain unpopulated placeholders (e.g., '[RESULTS HERE]', '[was/was not]', 'Overall, our results [were/were not] consistent with Crosby and colleagues’ original findings'). The shipped outcome_quote comes from a different, results-bearing version not present in this source text (and actually states that the original finding was replicated in their study, contradicting the shipped 'failed' label). Because the primary source text contains no actual outcome results, the replication outcome is undeterminable (consistent with the blind coder's cannot_be_determined assessment of missing outcome evidence, which maps to undeterminable with a null corrected_value).
